correctness.summary: Distinct positive degrees force degree sum at least n(n+1)/2, hence at least ceil(n(n+1)/6) triples. A modulo-6 link-graph induction realizes this bound for every n>=6, with degree set {1,...,n} except in residue classes 1 and 4 mod 6, where {1,...,n-2,n,n+1} supplies the minimal divisibility correction. A standalone verifier confirms the explicit construction through n=200.

limitations: The theorem requires no isolated vertices; the corresponding minimum when isolates are allowed is not claimed.
All minimum-size realizations are not classified up to isomorphism.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; older or differently indexed sparse degree-sequence literature remains a residual coverage risk.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 1992 irregular-uniform-hypergraph paper proves existence and discusses eliminating a possible isolate but does not give the checked fixed-order minimum-edge theorem. Broader uniform-hypergraph degree-sequence literature and recent dense irregular 3-graph realizability work were checked for stronger or equivalent coverage. Exact and synonymous searches did not locate this extremal formula or construction in the checked sources or current public archive.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result gives an exact sparse extremal formula for every admissible order together with an explicit recursive construction, and isolates the precise modulo-6 degree-sum correction needed for sharpness.
